newsitem.title: USA: Five rescued at sea after crash off Bahamas.
newsitem.headline: Five rescued at sea after crash off Bahamas.

text.p: A U.S. Coast Guard helicopter plucked five survivors of a small plane crash from the sea in the Bahamas Friday morning after they spent the night clinging to a life raft.
The five survivors, who were not identified but are believed to be from the United States, had spent more than 12 hours in the water when they were rescued, a spokesman for the Coast Guard said.

The group's Beechcraft 65 twin engine aircraft crashed into the ocean about 60 miles (80 km) west of Bain Airport on Mangrove Cay, off Andros Island in the Bahamas, at about 6:20 p.m. EDT (2220 GMT) on Thursday.

The group was en route from North Perry Airport in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, to Kingston, Jamaica, when the plane crashed. The plane disappeared from radar and plunged into the ocean when it lost an engine, the Coast Guard said.

The Coast Guard immediately launched two helicopters, a jet and a cutter to search for any survivors, but stopped after dark. The search resumed at dawn Friday, and the crew of a Coast Guard aircraft sighted the group at 7:49 a.m. EDT (1149 GMT).

When they were sighted, the aircraft's crew could see two people in the raft and two others clinging to its side. When a helicopter hoisted the group to safety, its crew discovered there were actually five people in the raft, everyone who had been on board the Beechcraft.
The five were dehydrated, but suffered no serious injuries. They were taken to Nassau, Bahamas, and flown to Opa Locka Airport outside Miami later Friday.
The Coast Guard spokesman said the downed Beechcraft's owner is from Plantation, Fla., a suburb of Fort Lauderdale.
